name: New Year and Cleaning
description: Limak is a little polar bear. His parents told him to clean a house before the New Year's Eve. Their house is a rectangular grid with h rows and w columns. Each cell is an empty square. He is a little bear and thus he can't clean a house by himself. Instead, he is going to use a cleaning robot. A cleaning robot has a built-in pattern of n moves, defined by a string of the length n . A single move (character) moves a robot to one of four adjacent cells. Each character is one of the following four: ' U ' (up), ' D ' (down), ' L ' (left), ' R ' (right). One move takes one minute. A cleaning robot must be placed and started in some cell. Then it repeats its pattern of moves till it hits a wall (one of four borders of a house). After hitting a wall it can be placed and used again. Limak isn't sure if placing a cleaning robot in one cell will be enough. Thus, he is going to start it w · h times, one time in each cell. Maybe some cells will be cleaned more than once but who cares? Limak asks you one question. How much time will it take to clean a house? Find and print the number of minutes modulo 10 9 + 7 . It's also possible that a cleaning robot will never stop — then print " -1 " (without the quotes) instead. Placing and starting a robot takes no time, however, you must count a move when robot hits a wall. Take a look into samples for further clarification.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers n , h and w ( 1 ≤ n , h , w ≤ 500 000 ) — the length of the pattern, the number of rows and the number of columns, respectively. The second line contains a string of length n — the pattern of n moves. Each character is one of uppercase letters ' U ', ' D ', ' L ' or ' R '.
output_specification: Print one line with the answer. If a cleaning robot will never stop, print " -1 " (without the quotes). Otherwise, print the number of minutes it will take to clean a house modulo 10 9 + 7 .
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 611F — New Year and Cleaning [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
